Early Wednesday morning contact with the terrorists was established, triggering a renewed firefight that remained ongoing as reported by PTI via Livemint's News Desk.
items.title: Gunfight in Kulgam as forces hunt escaped terrorist Lateef Bhat

items.summary: California has banned Waymo's autonomous vehicles from all state freeways, with the restriction issued last Wednesday. Jonathan Groveman, a spokesperson for the California Department of Motor Vehicles (DMV), stated in a statement that the ban bars Waymo from 'operating or testing its driverless vehicles on all California freeways,' characterizing them as posing an 'imminent hazard.' The measure follows three incidents involving Waymo's autonomous vehicles entering active construction closures south of San Francisco on 5 November, and another incident the next day, 6 November, that involved highway patrol vehicles on a highway in San Francisco. Video from the 6 November incident circulated widely on social media, showing a Waymo vehicle attempting to bypass California highway patrol vehicles conducting a traffic break. Groveman explained that 'the department determined that Waymo's driverless freeway operations pose an imminent hazard to public safety due to recurring incursions by its vehicles into active construction zones where construction workers, vehicles and equipment are present,' noting that similar incidents had previously occurred on 18 May. Waymo's autonomous vehicles expanded onto freeways and interstates around San Francisco, Los Angeles, and Phoenix last year; the Alphabet subsidiary operates the largest fleet of self-driving cars in the US. In response to the construction-zone encounters on US 101, a Waymo spokesperson said that 'the recent freeway construction zone encounters' did not 'involve any injuries or collisions,' adding that the company prioritized safety and had temporarily restricted freeway operations across its other operating markets while evaluating performance. The company stated it is working with the California DMV and other state officials to resume freeway operations, and continues to operate vehicles normally on California city streets. Groveman said the restrictions will remain in effect until 'Waymo demonstrates to the department that it has taken effective corrective actions to address the deficiencies that precipitated the restrictions.' The article does not report any injuries or collisions resulting from these incidents beyond Waymo's own statement, and provides no further detail on specific vehicle counts or incident outcomes.
items.title: California bans Waymo self-driving cars from freeways after construction-zone incidents

items.summary: As Cyclonic Storm Akvan intensifies over the central South and adjoining Westcentral Bay of Bengal, the India Meteorological Department (IMD) has issued a high-level weather warning for several southern states. The disturbance is expected to strengthen into a Severe Cyclonic Storm by Tuesday evening and a Very Severe Cyclonic Storm by the morning of November 19. Moving north-northwestward, Akvan is projected to cross the Andhra Pradesh and Yanam coasts between Nellore and Visakhapatnam—specifically near Tuni—around noon on November 20. Upon landfall, maximum sustained wind speeds are forecast at 120-130 kmph, with gusts reaching up to a devastating 145 kmph. The IMD has issued an “Orange Message” (Cyclone Alert) targeting the Andhra Pradesh and adjoining South Odisha coasts, directing authorities and residents in vulnerable regions to be prepared to take action. Under the system's influence, heavy to very heavy rainfall is expected, with isolated instances of extremely heavy rainfall exceeding 21 cm across Coastal Andhra Pradesh and Yanam on November 19 and 20. The agency also warns of a 1.0 to 2.0-metre surge above astronomical tide that could inundate low-lying areas in several districts during landfall, including Prakasam, Bapatla, Krishna, West Godavari, Konaseema, Kakinada, and Visakhapatnam. The peak surge is anticipated over Bapatla, Krishna, West Godavari, and Kakinada from morning to afternoon on November 20. The article was written by Arshdeep Kaur, a Senior Content Producer at Mint based in New Delhi.
items.title: IMD Issues Orange Alert as Cyclonic Storm Akvan Intensifies Over Bay of Bengal

items.summary: A US Army lieutenant colonel has been taken into US military custody following his arrest earlier this month by British counter-terror police on suspicion of spying for Russia. The serviceman, identified as Lt Col Brandon Carroll Tyner, aged 41 years old and serving in the US Army since 2008, was arrested near Gloucester last week under section one and section three of the National Security Act 2023, which relate to obtaining or disclosing protected information and assisting a foreign intelligence service. At the time of his arrest he had been based at Imjin Barracks in Innsworth, Gloucestershire, headquarters of Nato's Allied Rapid Reaction Corps, where he was said to be entrusted with sensitive information that would have been extremely damaging if leaked to Russia. Tyner had previously served in Afghanistan and Iraq before this posting. British police initially held him in London while the investigation proceeded; Assistant Commissioner Laurence Taylor, head of Counter Terrorism Policing, later confirmed a decision had been made to pass the investigation to US partners so it could be progressed there. The allegations were described by Taylor as extremely serious, with his arrest being the result of a long-running operation by MI5 in collaboration with the FBI. At the time of his arrest Russia said it had nothing to do with it; Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov told reporters on 10 November that he was unaware of what Tyner's case was connected to and added they have nothing to do with us. Detectives had sent a file to the Crown Prosecution Service for consideration, but at that stage both the Attorney General's Office in London and US authorities became involved before the decision was taken to transfer Lt Col Tyner into custody under US Uniform Code of Military Justice rather than standing trial in the UK. FBI director Kash Patel said an army officer was now in custody as the result of an espionage investigation and close cooperation between the bureau, the US Army and various UK partners, adding that this FBI has zero tolerance for anyone who betrays their oath to the United States or puts national security at risk. US Brig Gen Sean Stinchon added that the case should serve as a stark warning to any service member suspected of violating the oath they all take, stating whenever somebody is suspected of betraying the trust of fellow soldiers and jeopardising collective defence, it will be identified and justice served. The BBC understands Tyner's identity; figures such as his age and years of service are reported by that outlet rather than independently confirmed in this item.
items.title: US Army officer arrested in UK on spying suspicion taken into US military custody

items.summary: Police in the Philippines have charged Thomas Markle Sr, father of Meghan, Duchess of Sussex, with possession of and intent to distribute child sexual abuse material. The charges were filed on Monday, according to Cebu province prosecutor Graeme Elmido, who told the BBC that police had brought two counts of intent to distribute CSAEM (child sexual abuse and exploitation material) and one count of possession of CSAEM material. Earlier this month, Markle was separately arrested and charged in the US with possession of child sexual abuse material; the FBI said agents seized about 78 items from storage units he rented, including film negatives, slides and books that they allege contained such material. Markle, who is now in custody in the US, has previously denied the allegations, and the BBC says it has contacted his attorney for comment. Last month, Philippine police obtained a warrant to examine devices allegedly removed from Markle's former home in the country; four boxes of material including computers, phones, hard drives and old video tapes were handed to officers by Meghan's half brother Thomas Markle Jr. Markle Sr had initially been placed under house detention at his assisted living facility in Florida but was taken back into custody last week after prosecutors alleged he removed his ankle monitor. Meghan Markle has been estranged from her father since 2018, and the BBC reports she broke contact with him last year after telling him that she and the authorities knew he had abused young girls. In a statement shared earlier this month following the emergence of the allegations against her father, Meghan wrote: "I am deeply distressed... my thoughts are with any children who may have been harmed." She said she hoped it could be understood why she largely cut off contact from him and did not allow him to have contact with their children. The BBC has contacted Markle's attorney for comment but no response had been obtained at the time of reporting.
items.title: Thomas Markle Sr charged over child sex abuse material in Philippines

items.summary:
A Finshots piece evaluates what happened ten years after the November 2016 demonetisation, when Prime Minister Narendra Modi announced that ₹500 and ₹1,000 notes would no longer be legal tender. The author recalls watching the news break during dinner at home, with people lining up outside ATMs to withdraw ₹400 in cash because only ₹100 notes were available then; UPI had existed for barely three months but was not yet used widely. Notes worth about ₹15 lakh crore vanished overnight, and most of India's cash-dependent informal sector suffered as almost everything ran on scarce cash.

The article then examines each stated objective against the data. On black money: 99.3% of banned notes came back, with only about ₹10,720 crore missing; before the ban it was expected that roughly ₹4-5 lakh crore held as untaxed cash would not return, but this did not happen because people earning untaxed income often park wealth in real estate, gold or shell companies rather than keeping all of it as cash. The RBI board had also warned beforehand that demonetisation was unlikely to significantly impact black money and counterfeit notes.

On fake currency: the author disputes the claim linking cash-in-circulation magnitude directly to corruption levels, using Japan (a cleaner economy) with about 20% cash-to-GDP versus India's around 12%, which has stayed fairly stable despite UPI growth because GDP also grew and many transactions—real estate, weddings, tips, rural small-shop payments—still occur in cash. NPCI is planning a fee for UPI transactions above ₹2,000, which could push some shops back to cash. On counterfeits: RBI data shows counterfeit notes detected per crore fell from 70 in FY16 to 13 in FY26 overall; but focusing on the higher-denomination ₹500 note (where counterfeiting is most common), fakes rose from 0.3 to 20 per crore between demonetisation and now, though this uses only new notes so FY17 was a poor baseline. Comparing old versus current ₹500 notes instead shows counterfeits fell from about 167 to 20 per crore—suggesting the anti-counterfeit goal was largely met; yet fakes were never a huge problem as they formed a tiny fraction of total notes, and demonetisation cost an estimated 1.5-2% loss in economic output while hurting the informal sector.

On widening the tax net (an objective added later): filing returns jumped partly because cash deposits could now be traced to PAN records, but GST arrived in 2017 along with wider TDS use; new filers earned about ₹2.7 lakh on average, barely above the ₹2.5 lakh threshold at the time, and direct tax collections rose only slightly from 5.53% of GDP in FY17 to 5.86% the following year before falling to 4.78% by FY21, then reaching a high of 6.73% in FY25 after the pandemic.

The final verdict: demonetisation nudged people toward digital payments and brought more into the tax-filing system—though the pandemic was also a powerful force pushing contactless payments, which leave trails that can eventually expand the tax base—but curbing black money clearly failed; this would require stricter law enforcement and measures to plug loopholes letting people park undisclosed income in other assets or buy property with cash. The author ends by noting that until then… (an incomplete sentence). A Ditto term insurance advertisement follows, addressed to breadwinners about financial security if they are not around.

The article is a Finshots piece; the source text is marked untrusted.
items.title: Demonetisation's decade: promises versus outcomes in India

items.summary: Political activity is intensifying ahead of the 2027 Uttar Pradesh Assembly elections, with Congress requesting 181 seats from the Samajwadi Party as part of seat-sharing negotiations. The Samajwadi Party countered by pointing to Congress's poor performance in the 2022 Assembly polls, where it won only two seats, and emphasised that candidate winnability matters more than raw seat allotment. Leaders from both parties have agreed that the quality of candidates is more important than quantity for effectively challenging the BJP. Discussions between party officials are planned over three days in Delhi to finalise the seat-sharing arrangement and preserve the alliance. The article also notes separate political developments, including a clash between the BJP and Congress sparked by Rahul Gandhi's remarks about parental affection at Sonia Gandhi's book launch, as well as unrelated security operations involving Lashkar-e-Taiba commander Mohammad Latif Bhat in Kulgam and Jensen Huang's willingness to return to NVIDIA pending board approval. The article does not specify how many seats each party ultimately holds or the exact outcome of these negotiations beyond Congress's initial demand for 181 seats from the Samajwadi Party before the polls.
items.title: Congress Demands 181 Seats from Samajwadi Party Ahead of Uttar Pradesh Polls

items.summary: The article traces how air pollution in Delhi is pushing residents to leave the city, following two families. Mohammad Najir began collecting segregated door-to-door waste as a landfill worker at Bhalswa, one of three landfills in Delhi; over roughly two decades he watched that site grow into a mountain while his own health declined — first tuberculosis diagnosed in 2007 with eight months of medication, then asthma developing around 2019 whose symptoms worsened in the colder months. His wife Manoura Begum arranged for Najir to move to their ancestral village Madhubani in Bihar on the hope that cleaner air would help him; his breathing did improve somewhat but he could not work, and because Begum herself could not find employment there she returned alone to Delhi's Baprola area, leaving them separated. Around the same time, flower-seller Kalu moved out after his four-year-old son suffered frequent eye infections and a persistent cough that a doctor attributed to dust, pollution and vehicle emissions; unable to work in Rajasthan's Bhilwara district, he migrated about 1,700 km south to Bengaluru. These people are described as 'smog refugees' — those who relocate from polluted areas to cleaner ones for health reasons. In India most reported cases involve leaving Delhi, one of the world's most polluted capitals and among only between 50 and 100 'good' or 'satisfactory' air quality days per year over the last seven years. Such migrants are usually relatively privileged with financial means to move comfortably; more recently some lower-income households have made similar moves under considerable strain, though these cases remain far rarer. The costs for poorer families extend beyond money: Kalu had to remove his two older children from their government school in Delhi and has not yet enrolled them anywhere in Bengaluru because the nearest one is too distant. Occupational exposure compounds vulnerability — Begum and Najir worked with unsegregated wet-and-dry waste that released toxic fumes, especially in summer, alongside frequent garbage-site fires; doctors told Najir his tuberculosis and asthma were likely work-related to Delhi's pollution. A 2023 report by the Chintan Environmental Research and Action Group comparing 100 waste pickers, safai karamcharis and security guards with a control group found that 75% of workers had abnormal pulmonary function versus 45% in controls, 17% suffered severe lung diseases (none in controls), and 26% reported breathing difficulty. Dr Shiva Kant Misra of Shivani Hospital IVF in Kanpur, part of the Doctors for Clean Air movement, explained that carbon monoxide, ozone, dust and smoke producing PM 2.5 and PM 10 irritate lungs and can multiply symptoms, with women, older people and young children especially affected; a 2018 Agra study found traffic-related pollution raised respiratory morbidity in children, with asthmatic episodes 1.79 times more likely among those living near traffic — the same exposure Kalu's son faced while his parents sold flowers on footpaths all day. Leaving also carries recurring costs: Begum said families like hers must save at least two to three months of earnings before relocating and may face unemployment, as she did after an office job in Netaji Nagar closed; for Kalu the round trip between Bengaluru and Bhilwara now takes about three days each way versus one day from Delhi, so his family travels only around once every four months. The move has helped: Bengaluru recorded AQI between 65 and 90 across 2015 and 2025, and Kalu's son is healthier there; but for Najir most damage appears done — breathlessness reduced yet he remains dependent on medication. Experts note psychological tolls too: Arjun Kamdar of Cambridge University said the rich can whimsically escape pollution (for example to Shimla), whereas forced relocation rattle lower-income migrants' identities and social standing, since they left cities seeking better lives only to leave them again. For many sufferers, leaving is not even an option — Virender Kumar of the Waste Picker Welfare Foundation works with waste pickers near a polluting waste-to-energy plant at Ghazipur landfill where women have had premature deliveries; one study found high PM 2.5 during pregnancy linked to 13% premature births and 17% low birth weight, and Kumar has seen men with kidney and lung diseases — yet these workers, many from West Bengal and Assam without land back home, cannot envision earning or feeding themselves after returning, so staying is their only option; Begum similarly wonders where people would go and how long they can keep 'running' from the air.
items.title: Delhi's pollution is driving health-driven migration among waste collectors and street vendors — but escape remains out of reach for many

items.summary: Political activity is accelerating before the 2027 Uttar Pradesh Assembly elections, as both the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) and opposition parties ramp up their outreach efforts. A recent clash between the BJP and Congress arose from Rahul Gandhi's remarks about parental affection made at Sonia Gandhi's book launch; the BJP criticized him while Congress defended his comments.
