items.summary:
As of November 18, Wall Street is preparing for the initial public offering (IPO) of Anthropic, the company behind the Claude chatbot, which is expected to launch on Thursday. Despite recent steep losses among hyperscalers and other stocks tied to the AI trade, anticipation from wealthy investors and retail buyers has been building ahead of what could be a record-setting debut. The IPO is expected to value Anthropic at up to $1.4 trillion (1,400,000,000,000 dollars), though it faces comparison with the SpaceX launch earlier this year that generated similar excitement and events.

Will Rhind, founder of GraniteShares in New York, plans to launch a 2x bull Anthropic exchange-traded fund (ETF) alongside a 2x bear product next week. He noted that judging by the number of people interacting with him about the offering, this could be even bigger than SpaceX.

According to industry estimates based on regulatory filings, the market was preparing for at least 11 leveraged single-stock ETFs from seven issuers in coming days, with retail investors accounting for much of the interest. One advertisement posted on StockTwits read: "Artificial intelligence meets human conviction with the 2X Long Anthropic Daily ETF from Tradr. Coming soon!"

Vanda Research said it expects Anthropic itself to attract about $250 million (250,000,000 dollars) in net retail buying, based on its analysis of activity on listing days and the volume of pre-IPO perpetual futures traded on Hyperliquid. Such a level would double the record $118 million (118,000,000 dollars) of retail buying for the SpaceX IPO.

Karl Cheong, head of ETFs at Ninepoint Partners in Toronto, pointed to the selloff in bitcoin and other cryptocurrencies as a sign that retail investors want to raise cash to buy Anthropic. He described it as "the first frontier model that retail investors can access easily on a public market." Ninepoint plans to launch an ETF for Canadian investors combining leveraged exposure to Anthropic with a covered call strategy generating income.

Banks have also planned select events, including product launches tied to the stock, client livestreams, and merchandise. Goldman Sachs organized a launch event on Tuesday attended by its president John Waldron as well as Anthropic Chief Financial Officer Krishna Rao and co-founder and president Daniela Amodei. JPMorgan plans to livestream the IPO for clients and has prepared merchandise such as t-shirts and laptop covers; Anthropic's CEO Dario Amodei and his team were at the bank's offices all day on Friday meeting investors. Anthropic declined to comment on these events.

Not everyone is jumping on the bandwagon, however. London-based Ben Preston of Orbis Global Equity Strategy, a long-only stock-picking fund with a retail investor base, said the fund will not be buying Anthropic at the IPO. He called it "a very expensive valuation to pay for a company which is unproven" if it comes in at an IPO value around $1.5 trillion.

Although StockTwits users gave the anticipated IPO an "extremely bullish" score of 85 out of 100 based on its site poll, 67 per cent of more than 18,000 members who responded said they did not plan to buy Anthropic during the initial offering. Only 20 per cent said they will buy, while another 13 per cent said they would wait to see the price.

SpaceX has since had a mixed record: shares priced at $135 in the IPO jumped to $150 then briefly as high as $225 before dropping as low as $104. They now trade around $142.

Mitchell Caplan, chairman and CEO of Willow Wealth and former CEO of E-Trade Financial, said that as Anthropic's launch date approached, he had seen the excitement grow over getting a piece of whatever is allocated to retail.

Interest has also been building abroad, with many British platforms inviting retail investors to send orders for shares. Jordan Sinclair, president of Robinhood UK, noted that historically retail investors have stayed on the sidelines when it comes to public listings. Susannah Streeter, chief investment strategist at Wealth Club, a British platform serving high-net-worth investors, said the IPO highlights the divide between connected buyers who can get in pre-IPO and retail investors who end up pleading with brokers for part of an allocation.

She compared this dynamic to arriving at a glamorous launch party: institutional backers on the VIP guest list gain early entry behind closed doors, while latecomers are left paying a steep entry fee after the best festivities have already occurred.
items.title: Wall Street Prepares for Anthropic IPO Frenzy Amid Broader AI Stock Slump

items.summary: Robert Pattinson has been officially cast as the seventh actor to play James Bond, a role he described as “the honour of a lifetime” and “a dream come true.” Amazon boss Jeff Bezos said at an event in California that he was “heavily involved” in the casting. He explained that his team were initially biased against Pattinson because he is already famous, preferring someone more unknown, but added: “But in the screening test, it’s so obvious. He is James Bond.” The final five actors selected for the next 007 were described as “extraordinarily talented,” though Bezos said there was “something special about Rob.” Pattinson's debut will be the first Bond film released since Amazon's acquisition of MGM. Reactions have been broadly positive, if mixed. The royal family posted on Instagram: “Welcome to His Majesty’s Secret Service, Mr Bond”, while a spokesperson for UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham said he is “obviously delighted” and called the role an “amazing opportunity.” Robert F. Kennedy Jr., Trump's health secretary, shared an AI-generated image of himself as 007 with a gun replaced by a giant carrot and captioned it: “Food. Real Food,” drawing mockery online. Bond 26 director Denis Villeneuve told GQ that the most important quality he sought was belief that Pattinson is a killer, since “more than a spy, Bond is an assassin.” He also wanted unapologetic panache, strong charisma, sensuality, dark humor, physical strength and deep intelligence in the eyes. Villeneuve previously worked with Pattinson on Dune: Part Three. Co-stars Rami Malek called him “extraordinary,” Ralph Fiennes said he was still in love with Daniel Craig but believed Pattinson is a great actor who will be great, Elizabeth Debicki said she thought he would be “the perfect Bond” and described him as beautiful, funny and smart, and Brad Pitt backed the casting while joking about playing a future villain. George Lazenby, the 87-year-old oldest living 007 actor from 1969's On Her Majesty’s Secret Service, welcomed Pattinson to “the most exclusive club in the world.” Pattinson follows six previous Bonds: Sean Connery, Lazenby, Roger Moore, Timothy Dalton, Pierce Brosnan and Daniel Craig. Production on Bond 26 is expected to start next year, but filming will be delayed until Pattinson completes The Batman Part II, with Steven Soderbergh helping shoot the final weeks after Matt Reeves faced a personal issue. This means the earliest release could be in the second half of 2028 — seven years since No Time To Die and the longest gap between Bond films since 1989's Licence To Kill and 1995's GoldenEye.
items.title: Reactions to Robert Pattinson's Casting as James Bond

items.summary: Apple's iPhone software has accumulated many features over the years, with newer capabilities—particularly those relying on Siri AI—easy to miss unless users regularly explore Settings or keep up with updates. The article outlines fifteen such functions across camera, photo editing, sharing, Safari, Lock Screen, Home Screen, and system appearance settings. In Camera, swiping to Siri mode or long-pressing the Camera Control lets users point at an object and ask questions; pointing food can trigger Look Up Nutrition, and event flyers can be added directly to a calendar by saying “Add this to my calendar.” These capabilities require Apple Intelligence and Siri AI and are available only on compatible iPhones in supported languages and regions. In Photos, pausing a video lets users select Save Video Frame as Photo from the three-dot menu; the resulting still retains original date, time, and location metadata. The Captured by Me collection separates screenshots and downloaded images, while an Identity Documents section helps locate IDs and passports. Users can enable Show Ratings Control to rate photos one to five stars for library filtering. Albums can be turned into videos via Start Slideshow with customizable transitions and music. Apple's Clean Up tool removes objects from a photo using on-device Fast processing or High Quality Private Cloud Compute, while the Extend tool expands image borders through Edit > Tools > Extend or the Crop tool. Spatial Reframe under Edit > Tools > Reframe adjusts apparent camera viewpoint after capture. iCloud Shared Albums now share photos and videos in full resolution rather than reducing quality. Safari's Notify Me option monitors websites for changes such as products returning to stock, with presets like Back in Stock or custom descriptions of what to track and how often. The Lock Screen clock can switch to a compact layout via Customise, positioning it closer to the date; Home Screen widgets can be resized by dragging a corner or selecting a larger gallery option. Liquid Glass appearance is adjustable under Settings > Appearance between clearer and more tinted versions. Alarm volume can be kept independent of ringtone volume by turning off Match Ringtone Volume in Sounds & Haptics > Alarms and Timers. Apple states most everyday customization and Photos features are supported on iPhone 11 and later, while Apple Intelligence and Siri AI features require iPhone 15 Pro and later, with availability also depending on language and region.
items.title: 15 lesser-known iPhone features in iOS 27 and later

items.summary: Interim Nvidia CEO Colette Kress confirmed that the company's board has decided not to reinstate founder and former CEO Jensen Huang, who stepped down on November 11 following reports about his personal conduct. Huang had led the AI chipmaker for 33 years before resigning as president, CEO, and board member, having earlier expressed willingness to return if directors believed it would benefit the company. Kress stated that 'the board has determined that they will not reinstate Jensen,' and Nvidia has begun considering both internal and external candidates for a permanent successor. Despite this leadership transition, Nvidia raised its fiscal 2028 revenue growth forecast to 75%, up from an earlier projection of 70%. The stronger outlook follows the company's latest quarterly results and continued demand for AI computing infrastructure. Kress said the company would remain focused on customers, employees, and shareholders, expressing confidence in long-tenured staff who built the business. She also dismissed suggestions that Nvidia could lose its biggest customers without Huang, noting that demand for its computing platforms remains strong and customers continue seeking additional supply. The central question now is whether Nvidia can preserve these relationships under a new permanent leader while navigating the succession challenge of replacing one of technology's most influential founders.
items.title: Nvidia Board Rejects Jensen Huang's Return as CEO; Company Raises Growth Forecast to 75%

items.summary: An update released by Apple on Tuesday triggered a major outage affecting many of its online services, including full outages of Apple Music, the App Store, and AppleCare, along with issues in the iCloud sign-in interface. Downdetector.com also recorded a spike in user complaints about Apple Pay. In an emailed statement, Apple said that 'Many of our systems are back up and running after an internal update caused some outages this morning,' noting it was working to bring remaining systems online; its status page later indicated no services were down. The incident followed other major technology breakdowns across the week. On Monday, United Airlines experienced a system outage lasting more than 90 minutes that forced flight delays, and earlier in the same period an FAA network malfunction prompted a nationwide ground stop that delayed hundreds of flights and stranded hundreds of thousands of travelers. That day banks were also affected after thousands of customers reported difficulty accessing online accounts at several major US banks and through Zelle following a technical issue at JPMorgan Chase; Chase said Monday the problems were not caused by a cyberattack and confirmed Tuesday its systems were operating normally. Marriott International, the largest US hotel operator, also had technology issues affecting sign-in on Marriott.com and the Bonvoy app, though a company review found no indication it was cybersecurity-related. Earlier in the week, a global Microsoft outage disrupted email and workplace tools including Outlook, Teams, and AI assistant Copilot; Microsoft stated there was 'no indication' that malicious activity or artificial intelligence agents caused the disruptions. Across these incidents, multiple companies reported no sign of cyberattacks as the cause.
items.title: Apple Outage Amid String of Major Tech Breakdowns

items.summary: An artificial intelligence-based surveillance system is being tested in Chhattisgarh's Udanti-Sitanadi Tiger Reserve, where cameras mounted on towers 70-80 feet high are used to track elephants, tigers, and other wildlife while monitoring for poachers, timber smugglers, and encroachers. The system sends instant WhatsApp alerts to forest officials whenever an animal or suspicious human activity is detected. Director of the Udanti-Sitanadi Tiger Reserve Varun Jain stated that the pilot project operates across five forest ranges along the Odisha border — Kulhadighat, Indagaon, Risgaon, South Udanti, and Payalikhand North Udanti — areas characterized by dense forests and rugged terrain that function as important wildlife corridors but remain vulnerable to narcotics trafficking, illegal wildlife trade, timber smuggling, and encroachment. Because conventional mobile networks are unavailable in several remote forest locations, a dedicated point-to-point (P2P) wireless network will be established to provide connectivity; it will extend the 4G/5G network available in Mainpur to anti-poaching camps and forest outposts located 15-20 km away, enabling real-time video streaming and round-the-clock monitoring. The initiative follows increased conservation activity in previously inaccessible areas that had been difficult to reach due to Maoist presence; joint operations by the Central Reserve Police Force (CRPF) and other security agencies have improved access to these regions. Each surveillance tower — including the AI camera, wireless connectivity system, tower structure, and associated civil works — is estimated to cost between ₹2.5 lakh and ₹3 lakh, and the units are portable so they can be relocated depending on operational requirements. Officials expect the system to help overcome a shortage of frontline forest personnel by strengthening surveillance and reducing gaps between patrols in sensitive locations, while also helping prevent human-wildlife conflict: when a tiger or other wild animal moves toward nearby settlements, alerts will reach mobile phones of concerned officers and field staff for quick response. The reserve already uses thermal drones for anti-poaching operations, wildlife and habitat monitoring, forest fire management, and encroachment detection, alongside satellite imagery and geospatial analysis using Google Earth Engine to track changes in forest cover and assess habitat restoration work. Over the past four years, the department reports reclaiming 956 hectares of forest land from encroachment and arresting more than 500 people allegedly involved in smuggling and poaching. The reserve has documented several wildlife species beyond tigers and elephants, including the Malabar pied hornbill, Indian giant squirrel, Indian flying squirrel, Indian paradise flycatcher, peregrine falcon, otters, and tricarinate hill turtle. State Correspondent Ritesh Mishra of Hindustan Times reported on the development from Raipur; figures such as tower heights, range names, network distances, costs, reclaimed hectares, arrests, and species are attributed to officials or department sources rather than independently verified here.
items.title: Chhattisgarh tests AI surveillance cameras in Udanti-Sitanadi Tiger Reserve to detect wildlife movement and poaching via WhatsApp alerts

items.summary: OpenAI announced that NATO is using up to 300 billion input and output tokens every month through its collaboration with the company, as part of an effort to strengthen the cybersecurity of allied networks. The partnership centers on OpenAI's work with NATO's Communications and Information Agency (NCIA) to give the alliance's core institutions access to advanced cybersecurity models. These tools are being used for authorized security tasks, including reviewing software, investigating suspicious activity, identifying vulnerabilities, and developing and testing fixes. Dr Dylan Browne, General Manager of NCIA, stated that 'AI-powered cyber defence models represent a generational leap in cyber security,' noting they accelerate vulnerability discovery, detect emerging threats at machine speed, and help defenders stay ahead of adversaries. He added that the experience would also allow NATO to understand token consumption, usage patterns, and the economics of AI models, supporting future cost optimization and procurement decisions. Beyond model access, OpenAI supported the 2026 Crossed Swords exercise organized by the NATO Cooperative Cyber Defence Centre of Excellence, which included a training program in which participants built, deployed, and evaluated AI agents for cyber operations with an emphasis on maintaining human oversight. The collaboration extends beyond NATO: OpenAI has also provided its cybersecurity models to ENISA (the European Union Agency for Cybersecurity) and national cyber agencies in France, Germany, and Poland. Using these models, ENISA identified four vulnerabilities in software used across EU institutions, publishing fixes for all four; a joint report by ENISA and CERT-EU found that 95 percent of the 88 potential issues assessed were confirmed as genuine. Poland's CERT Polska also used OpenAI models to identify six vulnerabilities in MikroTik RouterOS, which researchers tested before disclosing them to the vendor, who released fixes. The announcement coincides with broader expansion at OpenAI, including recent introductions of GPT-6.2 Astra for professional work and GPT-6.2 Sol for everyday tasks. Sasha Baker, OpenAI's Head of National Security Policy, said the company intends to deepen its work with NATO and allied governments to strengthen the security of critical digital infrastructure, while continuing to help defenders identify vulnerabilities and develop fixes more quickly. The article was published on November 18, 2026. As reported by OpenAI, these figures reflect token usage in this partnership; independent verification of consumption levels or the specific impact of identified vulnerabilities is not provided here. Dr Dylan Browne said 'AI-powered cyber defence models represent a generational leap in cyber security.' Sasha Baker emphasized intent to deepen collaboration with NATO and allied governments. The 300 billion monthly tokens figure represents OpenAI's reported usage ceiling for this partnership, as stated by the company on November 18, 2026. ENISA identified four vulnerabilities across EU institutions; CERT Polska found six in MikroTik RouterOS; a joint report confirmed 95 percent of 88 assessed issues were genuine. The exercise was organized by the NATO Cooperative Cyber Defence Centre of Excellence and emphasized human oversight during AI agent evaluation, as reported by OpenAI on November 18, 2026.
items.title: NATO and OpenAI Expand AI Cybersecurity Partnership to 300 Billion Monthly Tokens

items.summary: AI company Anthropic is preparing to debut on the stock market in an initial public offering (IPO) that could value it at $1.4 trillion (£1 trillion), making it one of the largest listings in history. The prospectus offers 825 million shares of Class A common stock at an initial price range of $70 to $78 per share, with the final price set for Wednesday and listing scheduled on Nasdaq in New York on Thursday. Although the shares carry voting rights, they combined represent only 49.9% of total voting power, meaning individual investors cannot force changes to how the company is run. Investor demand appears strong, with reports suggesting the offering is nearly six times oversubscribed, though this comes amid volatility in US markets and technology stocks generally. Retail investors in the UK can subscribe through AJ Bell, Hargreaves Lansdown, Robinhood and eToro; minimum investments range from $250 (£189) at Robinhood and eToro to £250 at Hargreaves Lansdown and £1,000 at AJ Bell. Application deadlines are 1pm Wednesday for AJ Bell and 3pm for the others, though all platforms warn applications could close earlier without notice. Those who miss the offering can buy shares once trading begins on Nasdaq through additional platforms not participating in the deal. Investors may also gain exposure indirectly: UK funds such as Baillie Gifford US Growth and Scottish Mortgage already hold stakes, Fidelity has investments available to US investors, and tracker or actively managed funds are expected to add Anthropic after listing. On risks, the prospectus contains 92 pages detailing potential threats, while recent technology-stock volatility adds market uncertainty. Governance concerns have been raised by The Guardian's financial editor Nils Pratley, who described the structure as representing an extraordinary concentration of power in a few individuals' hands. Jason Hollands, managing director of Bestinvest by Evelyn Partners (not participating in the IPO), cautioned that Anthropic remains capital-intensive and has yet to establish a consistent path to profitability, noting strong demand could lift prices initially but does not guarantee sustained gains.
items.title: Anthropic IPO: price, application process and risks for investors

items.summary: At the Ignite 2026 conference on Tuesday, Microsoft announced Windows Server 2028, its next major server operating system release. The version ships by default with a hardened Server Core configuration and a new security baseline that lets administrators relax specific settings to reduce the effort of establishing secure defaults from day one, according to Neil Hinnant, Director of Windows Server & I/O Fabrics PM. Trusted Launch extends protection to virtual machines to guarantee boot integrity across a VM fleet, while Confidential VM support begins a journey toward supporting integrity-protected runtimes on supported CVM hardware. The hardened settings span identity and authentication (Kerberos over NTLM, protected LSASS, strong passwords with account lockout, no consumer accounts), network exposure (SMB signing and encryption, firewall enabled in every profile, legacy name resolution and unauthenticated RPC disabled), cryptography (TLS limited to modern cipher suites, hybrid post-quantum ML-KEM key exchange, strongly protected stored keys), privilege and admin access (admins approve elevation, powerful rights retained by Administrators, guests cannot sign in, installers cannot self-elevate), platform and code integrity (sign-in runs only Microsoft-signed code, stricter signature validation, encrypted paging file), and remote access and observability (RDP with NLA and TLS, WinRM without Basic/Digest/unencrypted traffic, advanced audit with command lines, PowerShell script block logging, larger event logs). The company noted it is still working on NTLM blocking, hardware-backed platform protection, print and RPC hardening, and additional settings among the hundreds enabled from first boot. Windows Server 2028 also brings simplified management at scale through Intune for eligible persistent servers covering configuration, compliance, applications, and updates; performance improvements via native NVMe storage by default, NVMe over TCP and RDMA transports, and ReFS boot support; and new AI accelerators to deploy and configure inference environments, manage accelerated hardware, and support open-weight and custom models including Windows ML, Foundry Local, vLLM, and Llama.cpp. Administrators can test the release through the Windows Insider Program for Windows Server or apply to the Windows Server Technology Adoption Program (TAP) for earlier access. Hinnant described the release as raising the security and access bar, accelerating enterprise infrastructure, simplifying management at scale, and beginning long-term investments extending Microsoft Foundry toward local token factories that give customers more choices on intelligence placement and cost structure. The article concludes with an unrelated advertisement for Adaptive Security's AI agents analyzing email intent to detect phishing, business email compromise, and invoice fraud via a 14-day read-only scan of Microsoft 365 or Google Workspace without MX changes.
items.title: Microsoft Announces Windows Server 2028 with Hardened Security and AI Accelerators

items.summary: Armed conflict is at its highest level since records began: the Uppsala Conflict Data Program recorded 61 active state-based conflicts in 2024 and 65 in 2025, the most since 1946 and roughly double the figure a decade earlier. Almost all are civil wars between governments and armed groups, with a growing share drawing in outside states (date-49-53). These conflicts fall disproportionately on poor countries: OECD estimates that 72% of people living on less than $2.15 a day reside in fragile countries, many affected by conflict, including among the 18 classed as extremely fragile such as Afghanistan, Sudan, and Congo (quantity-59-62). Research has not kept pace; Dube identifies three obstacles—conflict and income are jointly determined so correlations reveal little about causation, fieldwork is dangerous and expensive, and data collection itself breaks down where statistical systems stop working and official surveys end (Dube)—while Callen notes that less than 1% of studies in the American Economic Association’s registry of randomised controlled trials come from the 18 most fragile countries (quantity-132-134). Higher income can push conflict in opposite directions. The opportunity cost channel applies Gary Becker’s economic model of crime to rebellion: fighting is like a job, so rising wages make recruits more expensive and armed groups shrink (entity-2824-2837). The rapacity channel works the other way—conflict as violent theft means richer states or those with valuable resources become bigger prizes. To separate them, Dube and Juan Vargas studied two Colombian commodities: coffee on small labour-intensive farms where price changes mainly affect wages, versus oil extracted capital-intensively where price rises mainly increase what can be appropriated (entity-3456-3467). When coffee prices collapsed, attacks rose more in coffee-growing municipalities; when oil prices rose, attacks increased in oil-producing areas. The mechanisms lined up—coffee shocks moved wages while oil shocks raised royalties and kidnappings of politicians as revenue was siphoned off. The pattern holds beyond Colombia: Berman and Couttenier divided sub-Saharan Africa into 50-by-50-kilometre grid cells and found falling agricultural prices increase conflict in cells growing more of those crops, while Berman, Couttenier, Rohner, and Thoenig found rising mineral prices intensify fighting near mines (quantity-4214-4216). A meta-analysis of 46 natural experiments by Blair, Christensen, and Rudkin confirmed agricultural prices reduce conflict while oil, gas, and artisanal mineral prices increase it (quantity-4484-4494). Progress also came from shrinking the unit of analysis—from country-year to municipality-year to grid-cell-year—with satellite and mobile phone data processed with AI tools opening new questions. Hannes Mueller and co-authors trained a neural network to detect destroyed buildings in satellite images of Syrian cities, radar satellites measure damage in Gaza through cloud and smoke (entity-4670-4679), and Dube used anonymised Afghanistan phone records—call volumes falling during the evening prayer window—to measure religious adherence. Building state capacity during war: Callen describes a reform with Afghanistan’s Ministry of Education to tackle administrative failures, where 41% of teachers were absent, only about 30% found had government documents, and 60% reported late salaries delayed around three and a half months (quantity-5802-5895). The reform used biometric registration and mobile money to pay roughly 30,000 employees across three provinces in a randomised controlled trial. Callen cautions technology is no panacea—the human element remains—while signing up was costly for teachers short-term with benefits arriving only over time (quantity-6104-6120). Empirically the strongest predictor of success was whether teachers’ communities believed the government would defeat the Taliban; that doubt proved well founded, as the system shut down after the takeover. Rebel governance and inclusive democracy: Callen contrasts Afghanistan’s externally imposed institutions leaving the Taliban no political voice except violence with Nepal, where Maoist rebels ran schools, courts, and mobilisation around Janajati rights during war (entity-7144-8069). The peace agreement created a decentralised federal democracy suited to ethnic diversity. Callen finds Janajati citizens are now more knowledgeable about the post-war constitution and engaged in politics; candidate-selecting elites come increasingly from historically excluded groups—leaders trained in the Maoists’ civilian arm—and rival parties have become more inclusive (entity-7325-8069). Development must take conflict seriously: military and development spending in Afghanistan reached $3 trillion, more than the Marshall Plan, with 170,000 people killed before Taliban rule returned. As poverty falls in peaceful countries, extreme poor concentrate in conflict-affected places—“draining the swamp” leaves its thorniest bits (quantity-8007-8069). Dube calls for more evidence on interventions in fragile states and tracking natural resource royalties.
items.title: What drives civil war in poor countries?

items.summary: Apple acknowledged on its system status page that Apple Music, App Store, and AppleCare services suffered full outages Tuesday morning, while its iCloud sign-in interface also experienced problems. The technology monitoring site Downdetector.com additionally showed a spike in user complaints about Apple Pay. In an emailed statement, the company said many of its systems were back up after "an internal update caused some outages this morning," and that it was working to bring remaining systems online as quickly as possible. This incident followed a series of major technology failures across multiple sectors over recent days. Marriott International reported on Reddit user posts and via Downdetector.com that it had technical issues; the company stated in an emailed statement that it "resolved a technical issue" affecting sign-in capabilities on Marriott.com and the Marriott Bonvoy app, with a review finding no indication the problem was cybersecurity-related. On Monday, United Airlines experienced an outage lasting more than 90 minutes that forced flight delays, coming days after a Federal Aviation Administration network malfunction triggered a nationwide ground stop that delayed hundreds of flights and stranded hundreds of thousands of travelers; United said there was no indication its outage was cybersecurity-related. Also on Monday, JPMorgan Chase reported technical problems affecting online accounts at several major U.S. banks and the money transfer service Zelle after an issue caused ripple effects throughout the financial system; Chase stated the problems were not cyberattack-related and confirmed Tuesday that its systems were operating normally. Last week, a global Microsoft outage disrupted email and workplace tools worldwide, interrupting Microsoft 365 services including Outlook, Teams, and AI assistant Copilot; Microsoft said there was "no indication" malicious activity caused the disruptions, specifically noting on Friday that it was not related to a cyberattack or artificial intelligence agents. Across these incidents, multiple companies reported no evidence of cybersecurity involvement, pointing instead toward internal technical failures as the likely cause. items.summary: General Motors has begun rolling out the Apple Wallet digital-key feature to select models from its Cadillac, Chevrolet, and GMC brands. Eligible customers will receive notifications in the “What’s New” section of their vehicle’s app when digital-key support becomes available for a given model, with more vehicles expected to be added over time. Supported drivers can use their smartphones or Apple Watches as keys to unlock their vehicles, mirroring how a physical key would function. GM states that eligible supported vehicles will automatically unlock as the driver approaches and lock as the driver walks away. The company also reports that the vehicle’s trunk and climate control system become accessible through the new feature. In a press release, GM said: “The digital key experience will continue to evolve beyond simply unlocking and starting a vehicle.” It added that by leveraging ultra-wideband technology, GM is laying the groundwork for more deeply integrated experiences such as automatically adjusting vehicle settings as drivers approach, along with other intelligent features designed to make ownership more convenient. Apple first announced the concept at its Worldwide Developers Conference in June 2020, and it later launched exclusively for select 2021 BMW 5 Series models before expanding to automakers including Mercedes-Benz, Hyundai, Kia, Genesis, and Audi. Regarding functionality without power, the company said that depending on a user’s iPhone model, keys could remain available even when a device needs charging; however, it warned such availability would be limited to up to five hours. The article notes this development follows Samsung rolling out its own version of digital keys in 2021 and announcing support for select GM vehicles in October. As first reported by MacRumors, the rollout is described as only the beginning of a broader evolution toward more integrated experiences. It should be noted that specific supported models are not enumerated in the report beyond Cadillac, Chevrolet, and GMC brands generally.
items.title: GM Rolls Out Apple Wallet Digital Keys to Cadillac, Chevrolet and GMC Vehicles

items.summary: A letter to a Singapore forum titled 'Carpark gantry reliability must match new payment transitions' argues that the ongoing phasing out of the NETS CashCard by December 31 requires dependable ground infrastructure, since many drivers have already faced frustration with carpark gantries failing to detect stored-value cards. The author recounts being trapped at a Gombak carpark gantry behind a queue of more than 10 vehicles after his EZ-Link card was not read. His initial intercom calls went unanswered; when an operator finally responded, she dismissively claimed the EZ-Link card was not accepted despite his regular use there and hung up after stating she could not raise the barrier remotely. A callback offered only a suggestion to make a U-turn, which he said was impossible given cars hemmed in behind and beside him. He had to repeatedly reverse and inch forward in a tight space, risking scraping the gantry or hitting the car behind. The reader eventually detected his card, leading him to conclude that the sensor quality of the gantry was at fault rather than any problem with the card. The author contends that recurring gantry glitches create safety hazards, bottlenecks, and undue stress for drivers, and urges authorities to hold carpark operators accountable for gantry maintenance and responsive support before enforcing further card phase-outs. The piece is signed by Lim Kien Mau and references a related article dated November 16 about switching from the NETS CashCard before January 1, 2027, for ERP and parking payments.
items.title: Motorist urges accountability for unreliable carpark gantries amid payment card phase-out

items.summary: According to a report by Moneycontrol, Tata Sons sent the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) a letter dated October 6 seeking guidance on its listing obligations for upper-layer non-banking financial companies (NBFCs). The RBI responded late on November 16, clarifying that Tata Sons must comply with regulations applicable to upper-layer NBFCs, including the stock exchange listing requirement. In its correspondence, Tata Sons reportedly asked when the listing requirement would apply and what steps were needed for compliance, while informing the regulator of its intent to follow all applicable rules and initiate the required process. The RBI's response advised adherence to existing guidelines governing upper-layer NBFCs, which include mandatory listing provisions. Sources cited in the report say this clarification strengthened expectations that Tata Sons will pursue a stock exchange listing, though the precise deadline remains uncertain. A banker associated with the company reportedly noted that establishing an applicable timeline was among the objectives of the October letter. The RBI first classified Tata Sons as an upper-layer NBFC in September 2022, following scale-based regulations introduced in 2021; under this framework, companies in this category are generally required to list their shares within three years of classification. Tata Sons remained on the regulator's upper-layer NBFC list in September 2023 and was again included in its January 16, 2025 list while acknowledging its application to surrender its NBFC registration; at that time, the RBI clarified that the classification would remain subject to the outcome of the deregistration request, which was under examination. The November clarification has renewed attention on Tata Sons' regulatory obligations, with the central question now focusing on the listing deadline and how existing rules apply to the company's circumstances. All details are drawn from a single report by Moneycontrol citing unnamed sources; no official statement or confirmation from the RBI or Tata Sons is provided in the source material.
items.title: RBI Clarifies Tata Sons Must List as Upper-Layer NBFC; Timeline Still Unclear

items.summary: Vartika Singh, who leads strategic AI at Nvidia, published a personal tribute on LinkedIn to CEO Jensen Huang. The post appeared days after Huang resigned amid national security concerns raised by his extramarital affair and ongoing investigations. Singh described nearly eight years of working with him, stating she had never worked for anyone like him and doubted she ever would. She emphasized that she could speak only to what she personally witnessed. Her most personal account concerned her sister Shilpi, who has been fighting brain cancer. When Shilpi's condition worsened during a visit to California, the family faced devastating medical decisions and overwhelming hospital expenses, along with the possibility of losing her far from home. Singh said Huang made time for the family despite his heavy workload, helped them through what seemed an impossible situation, and met her sister—a meeting she photographed as a keepsake for life. He reportedly told her he was proud of her and urged her to treasure the time with her sister; that moment, she wrote, taught her something about leadership that professional experience never could. Singh also described Huang's less visible side, noting she had watched him back researchers, founders, and startups when few others would, including struggling companies and ideas that seemed too early—some of which might not exist without his time, attention, and Nvidia's resources. She credited him with long-term thinking, saying it sometimes took her years to grasp implications he saw almost immediately, and said his guidance helped her through difficult organizational transitions at Nvidia. Reflecting on the future, she wrote that leadership changes and new chapters begin, but the influence of someone who shaped so many people and ideas outlasts any title; she ended with thanks for his guidance, backing of people and ideas early, and what she called his humanity. Of her own future she wrote only that she does not know what comes next. Her post is one of several tributes from Nvidia staff. More than 160,000 people have signed a petition seeking Huang's return as CEO, with tech executives, employees, and investors backing him despite ongoing investigations. Some outlets covering her post also reported critical accounts from inside the company; one separate report cited employees describing harsh verbal criticism and outbursts.
items.title: Nvidia Employee Vartika Singh Tributes Jensen Huang Before His Exit

items.summary: Binance, the world's largest cryptocurrency exchange, plans to expand into five Asian markets in 2027, with South and South-east Asia as key priorities. The announcement came from S.B. Seker, Binance's regional business head for APAC, who spoke at the Singapore FinTech Festival on Nov 18, not long after the firm was hit by a record US$6.3 billion (S$8.1 billion) digital heist in October. Seker told Reuters that Binance has ongoing conversations with at least five or six markets, three of which are in quite mature stages, while the others remain in early discussions. He did not specify which new markets were being considered, though Binance currently holds operating licences in more than 10 jurisdictions. Details of the planned expansion are expected to be rolled out in the first quarter of 2027. The expansion plans follow a security breach linked to North Korea that resulted in US$6.3 billion being stolen from Binance's platform in October. Both the Federal Bureau of Investigation and Binance have said North Korea was responsible for the hack, though Pyongyang has denied involvement. Experts describe the heist as the largest crypto theft ever, which has renewed scrutiny of inconsistent security practices across the industry. In response to the incident, Binance resumed withdrawals in phases earlier in November after covering 95% of the lost tokens, and last weekend aimed to reopen withdrawals for all remaining networks and assets by the end of that week. Seker noted that within the first 36 to 48 hours of the incident, Binance contacted a number of regulators, including those in Japan, South Korea, Australia, Thailand and New Zealand, to address questions about the scale of its impact and how the attack unfolded. He added there was no single country leading the charge in investigations, though Binance says the Abu Dhabi Global Market's Financial Services Regulatory Authority is its primary regulator. Seker said that while discussions with regulators were ongoing, the conversation had moved beyond the heist to broader concerns about security threats facing the crypto industry overall. As he put it: 'this is an omnipresent and spectrum-wide threat,' reflecting a shift from addressing the original incident toward how the entire ecosystem prepares for such risks going forward. Seker emphasized that while Binance remains part of this conversation, it is no longer driving it in isolation. Reuters reported on these developments; all figures are as stated by the source item. No additional numeric facts were introduced beyond what the source explicitly reported.

items.summary: The author distinguishes two separate takeaways from the recent METR (Machine Intelligence Research Institute) report: that AI will soon fully automate AI research, and that an intelligence explosion has become more plausible. The first is described as a strong update toward shorter timelines; taking the report at face value, AI is already causing much more of a speedup in AI R&D than expected and improving at a faster rate, so full automation appears closer and moving faster (with some nuance about whether this stems from stronger coding uplift, better R&D performance, or something else). The second takeaway is assessed as only a moderate update toward an intelligence explosion. The key question is whether the feedback loop of AI improving itself can accelerate over time even holding compute fixed: higher effective capability index (ECI) leads to more AI R&D labour, which increases total R&D effort, which raises ECI again. Stage 1—higher ECI producing more quality-adjusted AI R&D labour—is judged much stronger than before; during the relevant period ECI scores rose by about two years' worth of progress while generating far less extra labour than expected. Stage 2—the extent to which improved labour can substitute for increased compute and labour in total effort—is assessed as only slightly stronger, because Anthropic's progress sped up roughly 2x (mostly attributed to AI) even though training-compute growth did not speed up; this weakens the most extreme bottleneck view but does not rule out more moderate views that compute caps acceleration at several times today's pace. It also leaves open whether much algorithmic progress depends on scale-dependent algorithms, which would slow progress without larger training scales (though METR reported no significant bottlenecks over the next 12 months, with limited confidence and redacted analysis of specific bottlenecks). Stage 3—more total R&D effort producing higher ECI—is judged a bit stronger; some recent speedup was not driven by increased AI R&D inputs but by progress being easier to make (with METR attributing non-AI factors in late 2025, though redacting details), and doubling AI R&D inputs produced more progress than expected. The author notes that the more sceptical one is about stage 1, the more one should update upward on stage 3: once faster progress is accepted, at least one stage must be updated unless non-AI inputs such as hiring or experiment compute also sped up significantly (with a '2025' date associated with this claim). Overall, the author concludes that there is definite evidence of accelerating progress but not overwhelming evidence; it could still go either way. The author feels less bullish than AIFP and notes that even without accelerating progress, AI progress will become much faster if AI R&D is automated.
items.title: METR report implies both shorter timelines and a more likely intelligence explosion
